title: Suns keeping breakout guard Collin Gillespie on 4-year, $48 million deal: Source
content:
The Phoenix Suns and point guard Collin Gillespie have agreed to a four-year, $48 million contract in principle, a team source confirmed to The Athletic.

ESPN’s Shams Charania was the first to report the deal.

The new deal will have no player or team options, a team source said. Such security is well-earned for Gillespie, who signed three two-way contracts between stints with the Suns and Denver Nuggets before becoming a key piece of Phoenix’s long-term future.

In 80 regular-season games, he averaged 12.7 points as a third-year pro after posting a scoring average of 4.9 in his first 57 appearances. The 26-year-old averaged 10.5 points in Phoenix’s first-round series against the defending champion Oklahoma City Thunder, which ended in a Thunder sweep.

Gillespie’s value grew when Phoenix needed him in the starting lineup. In 58 regular-season starts, he scored 13.3 points, 4.2 rebounds and 4.7 assists. Overall, he proved to be a consistent positive for the Suns, who saw a net-rating swing of 5.9 points per 100 possessions based on Gillespie’s presence.

Gillespie shined as a scorer, passer and teammate throughout the season. In February, as the rest of the basketball world was adjusting to Gillespie’s sudden turn as an impact player, the 6-foot-1 guard scored a career-high 30 points with eight 3-pointers and 10 assists in a 130-125 win over the Portland Trail Blazers. The performance prompted Devin Booker — the franchise’s leading scorer — to declare that everyone else may have been caught by surprise, “but nobody in this locker room.”

Among the most vital areas of Gillespie’s growth came as a catch-and-shooter player. Among all Suns, he trailed only Royce O’Neale (492) for the team lead in points on such shots, finishing with 401, according to NBA.com. He did it efficiently, too, shooting 46.1 percent overall on catch-and-shoot looks and 45.8 percent on such 3s. The Suns finished sixth among all teams in catch-and-shoot points, ranking sixth and eighth in overall and 3-point percentage, respectively.

Gillespie went undrafted in 2022 after five years at Villanova that included a national championship as a freshman. He signed with Denver that summer, but then broke his leg while playing in a pickup game at his alma mater and didn’t suit up for the Nuggets until the 2023 NBA Summer League in Las Vegas.

Three years later, he grew into a critical piece of the Suns’ surprise return to Western Conference playoff contention. Under first-year head coach Jordan Ott, the Suns made the playoffs for the fifth time in six seasons despite starting the year with low expectations. Ott was their fourth coach in as many years, but his ability to maximize players like Gillespie helped him finish fifth in NBA Coach of the Year voting.
